speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; please tell me, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and is the pain located specifically in your chest or elsewhere?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture).

Based on the history of forceful vomiting after alcohol consumption followed by sudden chest pain and choking, I am highly concerned about an esophageal tear. Please confirm if you have any shortness of breath, fever, or a history of connecting the vomiting specifically to the onset of the chest pain?
